facts.statement: Bonapartenykus is an extinct alvarezsauroid dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous of the Allen Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: Bonapartenykus (meaning "José F. Bonaparte's claw") is an extinct genus of alvarezsauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian–Maastrichtian) of what is now the Allen Formation of the Río Negro Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The only known species, Bonapartenykus ultimus, was found with two incomplete eggs and eggshells belonging to the oogenus Arriagadoolithus.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Bonapartenykus ultimus, known from a partially articulated, incomplete skeleton that was found in close association to two incomplete eggs and several clusters of eggshells belonging to the oogenus Arriagadoolithus.

facts.statement: The genus Bonapartenykus was named in 2012.
facts.quote: Bonapartenykus was named in 2012.

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus is the largest known member of the Alvarezsauroidea clade, with an estimated length of 2.5 to 3.3 meters and a weight of 43 to 72 kilograms.
facts.quote: It has an estimated length of 2.5 - 3.3 m and weight of 43 - 72 kg, making it the largest member of the clade Alvarezsauroidea.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton associated with eggs was collected from approximately 30 square meters of fluvial sandstone in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: A partial skeleton of a theropod with eggs was collected in a surface of approximately 30 m2 in fluvial sandstones of the upper Allen Formation in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The species was redescribed and named in 2012 by Federico L. Agnolin, Jaime E. Powell, Fernando E. Novas, and Martin Kundrát.
facts.quote: The specimen was later redescribed and named in 2012 by Federico L. Agnolin, Jaime E. Powell, Fernando E. Novas and Martin Kundrát.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a mid-dorsal vertebra, scapulocoracoids, leg bones, and two eggs found less than 20 centimeters from the skeleton.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MPCA, 1290, consists of a mid-dorsal vertebra, both scapulocoracoids, left tibia and femur, left pubis articulated with the pubic peduncle of the ilium, the anterior blade of the left ilium, and two partially preserved eggs that were separated from the holotype by less than 20 cm (7.9 inches).

facts.statement: The eggs found with the skeleton were unique enough to be named Arriagadoolithus and classified in the new oofamily Arriagadoolithidae.
facts.quote: The eggs of Bonapartenykus were considered unique enough for them to be given a new parataxonomic name, Arriagadoolithus, which was classified in a new oofamily, the Arriagadoolithidae, so named for the owner of the site where the discovery was made.

facts.statement: The genus name Bonapartenykus honors Argentine paleontologist José F. Bonaparte and combines it with the Latin word for claw.
facts.quote: The generic name, Bonapartenykus, is derived from the Argentinean paleontologist José F. Bonaparte and the Latin word "onykus" (claw).

facts.statement: In 2025, researchers described additional alvarezsaurid material from the Salitral Ojo de Agua locality as possibly belonging to Bonapartenykus ultimus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Meso and colleagues described various alvarezsaurid material first reported in the late 2000s from the same formation, specifically within the Salitral Ojo de Agua locality, as cf. Bonapartenykus ultimus.

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus is distinguished by features such as specific laminae on vertebrae, a deflected coracoid with grooves, fused scapulocoracoids, a notched scapula, and a fused ilium and pubis.
facts.quote: Bonapartenykus can be distinguished from other alvarezsauroids based on the presence of spinopostzygapophyseal laminae that end abruptly above the postzygapophyses of the mid-dorsal vertebrae; the underside portion of the coracoid being strongly deflected towards the middle and decorated with delicate but abundant grooves as in Xixianykus; fused scapulocoracoids as in Ceratonykus; scapula with a very wide notch on the posterior margin of the bone; and a fused ilium and pubis.

facts.statement: Unique features of Bonapartenykus include an enlarged ischial peduncle on the pubis and a concave triangular surface on the distal pubic shaft.
facts.quote: Other autapomorphies of the taxon include an enlarged ischial peduncle of the pubis and the presence of a concave triangular surface located medially on the distal pubic shaft.

facts.statement: Unlike some other alvarezsaurids, the vertebrae of Bonapartenykus have a deeply concave cranial articular surface that might be procoelous.
facts.quote: Unlike Haplocheirus and Patagonykus, the centrum has a cranial articular surface that is deeply concave with a sharp bony margin that surrounds it, which might be procoelous.

facts.statement: The coracoid of Bonapartenykus is extremely elongate with an acute end that restricted its articulation with the sternum.
facts.quote: The coracoid is extremely elongate and ends at an acute end which restricted articulation with the sternum.

facts.statement: Based on its skeletal structure, Bonapartenykus likely had a flat and wide breast.
facts.quote: Alvarezsaurids like Bonapartenykus may have had a flat and wide breast based on a combination of characteristics like a continuous subhorizontal surface with formed by the medial deflection of the coracoids with the sternal plate.

facts.statement: The distal end of the pubic shaft in Bonapartenykus features a rounded pubic boot on its rear margin.
facts.quote: The pubic boot appears to be rounded in side view on the rear margin.

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus possesses a strongly fused pubic pedicle and a reduced cuppedicus fossa, characteristics unique among alvarezsaurids.
facts.quote: The pubic pedicle is also strongly fused with the pubis, which is a characteristic unique among alvarezsaurids, along with a reduced cuppedicus fossa.

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus had a very short and robust tibia with a shaft bowed towards the sides.
facts.quote: The tibia is very short and robust, while the tibial shaft is bowed towards the sides.

facts.statement: Agnolin et al. (2012) originally classified Bonapartenykus as a member of the clade Patagonykinae within the family Alvarezsauridae, making it the sister taxon to Patagonykus.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Agnolin et al. (2012) originally placed Bonapartenykus within Alvarezsauridae, within the clade Patagonykinae as sister taxon to Patagonykus.

facts.statement: Analyses by Xu et al. (2018) recovered Bonapartenykus as a basal alvarezsauroid that was not part of the Alvarezsauridae family and was more primitive than Patagonykus and Achillesaurus.
facts.quote: However, Xu et al. (2018) and subsequent analyses using their dataset recovered it as a non-alvarezsaurid alvarezsauroid, more basal than Patagonykus and Achillesaurus.

facts.statement: Meso et al. (2025) re-analyzed the bones and recovered Bonapartenykus as a patagonykine within the Alvarezsauridae, supporting the earlier classification by Agnolin et al. (2012).
facts.quote: In their 2025 description of bones they referred to Bonapartenykus, Meso et al. recovered it as a patagonykine within the Alvarezsauridae, similar to the initial description by Agnolin et al. (2012).

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Bonapartenykus is Alvarezsauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Alvarezsauroidea

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Bonapartenykus are found in the upper Allen Formation, dated to the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Bonapartenykus is known from fluvial sandstones of the upper Allen Formation which have been dated to the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Bonapartenykus lived alongside diverse fauna including sauropods like Bonatitan, hadrosaurids like Bonapartesaurus, the abelisaurid theropod Quilmesaurus, and the pterosaur Aerotitan.
facts.quote: The fauna of the Allen Formation consists of the titanosaur sauropods Bonatitan, Menucocelsior, Panamericansaurus, Rocasaurus and an indeterminate species of Aeolosaurus, the hadrosaurid ornithopods Bonapartesaurus, Kelumapusaura, Lapampasaurus and Willinakaqe, the nodosaurid Patagopelta, the abelisaurid theropods Niebla and Quilmesaurus, the large unenlagiid paravian Austroraptor, the avialans Lamarqueavis and Limenavis, the azhdarchid pterosaur Aerotitan, the rhynchocephalian Lamarquesaurus, and the plesiosaur Kawanectes.

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Bonapartenykus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3

facts.statement: Meso et al. (2026) published a redescription of the anatomy of the holotype specimen of Bonapartenykus ultimus.
facts.quote: Meso et al. (2026) redescribe the anatomy of the holotype specimen of Bonapartenykus ultimus.

rejected.quote: The specific name, ultimus, is derived from the Latin word "ultimus" (latest), as it is one of the geologically youngest alvarezsaurids from South America.
